Prevention: Destroy weeds early as they are attractive to ovipositing female cutworm moths.
Plough the soil before and after cropping cycle to kill cutworms or expose them to predators.
Intercrop tomato with onion or garlic every 10 to 20 rows to repel cutworms.
Protect stems of tomatoes from cutworms with protective collars made of plastic or cardboard cups, or made of cut plastic bottles, pushed into the soil around the seedling
Monitoring: Cutworms are 2 to 4 cm long larvae, and dark grey- brownish (= soil colour).
They are about 0.5 to 1 cm thick and very soft.
The big larvae cut the stem below or at the soil surface.
Young larvae feed on lower leaves, leaving perforations.
Search for larvae in nurseries and in the main field until a few weeks after transplanting.
Larvae can be found in the soil near the plant up to a depth of 5 cm.
Young larvae may also be on the leaves of seedlings.
Cutworms only feed at night, thus search at night or early in the morning.
If you find 1 to 2 cutworms per 20 to 30 plants or if you expect damage from previous cropping season experience, then consider action through green direct control.
During mass outbreaks (= non-normal according to long year experiences = uncountable numbers) action must be taken in form or green and yellow direct control.
Listen to alerts from local radio, newspapers and plant doctors
Direct Control: Apply ash around the seedling (mainly applicable in small plots).

Hot pepper spray (soak 30 to 40 chopped hot peppers or 1/2 l hot pepper powder in 10 l warm water (not boiling); let liquid steep for 24 h; remove pepper rests and dilute with 10 l cold water; add 20 (0.001 l) drops of dishwashing liquid (soap).
Spray in the evening directly to the soil around the stem of seedlings or young plants.
When, after sprays, still cutting of seedlings occurs, search for the larvae in the upper 5 cm of soil near the cut plants (particularly in the early morning) and collect them.
Restrictions: Spray in the evening directly to the soil around the stem of seedlings or young plants, because cutworms are active at night.
